title: Responsible Algorithmic Governance in Digital Platforms: A Keyword Co-Occurrence Map of Trust, Fairness, Accountability, and Privacy Research
content: Algorithmic systems are increasingly mediating interactions on digital platforms, yet research on their responsible governance is scattered across multiple disciplines. This study maps this field by analyzing the co-occurrence of keywords (VOSviewer) in 1,382 records from the Web of Science Core Collection from 2021 to 2026, assigning each record to a cluster based on a term-based score. A term-based relevance check identifies explicit e-commerce terms in 118 records (8.5%) and terms specific to recommendation systems in another 60; 1,361 (98.5%) contain at least one term related to e-commerce, recommendation systems, or platforms. Five clusters emerge: responsible AI governance (n = 311), trust and adoption on platforms (n = 58), explainable predictive analytics (n = 123), algorithmic accountability and fairness (n = 371), and privacy, bias, and security (n = 42). Another 477 records (34.5%) fall equally into two or more clusters; in these cases, accountability and fairness represent points of overlap. Scientific output is concentrated in recent years, with 48% of the records published in 2025. The map is descriptive in nature: it is based on a single database and the co-occurrence of terms, and the gaps identified are observations that need to be tested, not theories.
